This page lists Guardana's 59 built-in rules in 17 threat classes, with each rule's ID, title, default severity, and command. The `scripts/generate_docs.py` script builds the page from the installed rules and a class file and stops if any built-in rule has zero or multiple classes. Each rule checks for part of a threat, with [detection limits](detection-limits.md) explaining what findings prove and [taxonomy coverage](taxonomy-coverage.md) showing framework mappings.

| Threat | Rules | Runs with |
|---|---|---|
| Unsafe model and dataset loading | 8 | `scan` |
| Unsafe code in projects | 3 | `scan` |
| Risky dependencies | 2 | `scan` |
| Insecure downloads | 1 | `scan` |
| Model and dataset provenance gaps | 2 | `scan` |
| Hardcoded secrets | 1 | `scan` |
| Prompt injection and jailbreaks | 4 | `probe` |
| Agents steered by untrusted content | 3 | `probe` |
| Hidden instructions and tool manifest changes | 3 | `scan`, `probe` |
| System prompt and tool schema leaks | 2 | `probe` |
| Secrets and cross-tenant data leaks | 4 | `probe`, `analyze-trace` |
| Agent actions beyond authorization | 5 | `probe`, `analyze-trace` |
| Unbounded output and costly requests | 2 | `probe` |
| Unauthenticated chat inference | 1 | `probe` |
| MCP access and registry weaknesses | 10 | `probe` |
| A2A card and access weaknesses | 3 | `probe` |
| Delegation beyond granted authority | 5 | `analyze-trace` |

## Unsafe model and dataset loading

Guardana checks for dangerous pickle opcodes, Keras Lambda layers, SavedModel filesystem operators, risky model file and ONNX constructs, chat templates enabling code execution, and remote or custom code on load.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.supply_chain.pickle_opcode` | Dangerous pickle opcode (arbitrary code on load) | CRITICAL | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.supply_chain.keras_lambda` | Keras Lambda layer (arbitrary code on model load) | HIGH | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.supply_chain.saved_model_ops` | TensorFlow SavedModel filesystem operator | MEDIUM | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.supply_chain.model_format` | Risky construct in a non-pickle model file format | HIGH | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.supply_chain.onnx_graph` | Risky construct in an ONNX model graph | HIGH | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.supply_chain.chat_template` | Chat template carries a code-execution gadget | CRITICAL | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.supply_chain.remote_code` | Remote code execution enabled on model/dataset load | HIGH | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.supply_chain.remote_code_config` | Model config requests custom-code execution on load | HIGH | `scan PATH` |

## Unsafe code in projects

Guardana checks for unsafe model or deserialization loader calls, dynamic code or shell execution sinks, and dangerous notebook cell payloads.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.supply_chain.dependency_risk` | Unsafe model/deserialization loader call | HIGH | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.supply_chain.code_execution` | Dynamic code or shell execution sink | HIGH | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.supply_chain.notebook_payload` | Dangerous payload in a notebook cell | HIGH | `scan PATH` |

## Risky dependencies

Guardana checks for known malicious dependencies, install-time payloads, and imports of unknown packages.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.supply_chain.malicious_dependency` | Known-malicious dependency or install-time payload | HIGH | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.supply_chain.hallucinated_package` | Import of unknown package (possible slopsquat lead) | MEDIUM | `scan PATH` |

## Model and dataset provenance gaps

Guardana checks for unpinned model downloads, possible model license risks, dataset loader scripts, and unpinned training datasets.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.supply_chain.provenance` | Model provenance: unpinned download or risky license lead | MEDIUM | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.training.dataset_integrity` | Training-data integrity gap (loader script or unpinned dataset) | MEDIUM | `scan PATH` |

## Prompt injection and jailbreaks

Guardana checks for instruction overrides, jailbreaks using persona overrides and encoded content, gradual multi-turn jailbreaks, and indirect prompt injection through retrieved documents.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.prompt.injection.ignore_previous` | Prompt injection via instruction override | HIGH | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |
| `guardana.prompt.jailbreak.dan_style` | Jailbreak via persona override and encoding smuggling | HIGH | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |
| `guardana.scenario.gradual_jailbreak` | Gradual multi-turn jailbreak | HIGH | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |
| `guardana.scenario.indirect_injection` | Indirect prompt injection via a retrieved document | HIGH | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |

## Agents steered by untrusted content

Guardana checks for agents following instructions in tool results, poisoned memory steering later sessions, and applications following instructions planted in retrieved documents.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.agent.tool_result_injection` | Agent obeys an instruction found in a tool result (confused deputy) | CRITICAL | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |
| `guardana.agent.memory_poisoning` | Poisoned memory steers the agent in a later session | CRITICAL | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |
| `guardana.retrieval.poisoned_document` | The application followed an instruction planted in a retrieved document | HIGH | `probe --url URL --model MODEL --fixtures FILE` |

## Hidden instructions and tool manifest changes

Guardana checks for hidden instructions in files agents read, MCP tool descriptions, and live MCP tool manifests, as well as changes to live manifests.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.prompt.hidden_instructions` | Hidden instruction smuggled into a file an agent reads as context | HIGH | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.prompt.mcp_tool_poisoning` | MCP tool description carries a hidden instruction (tool poisoning) | HIGH | `scan PATH` |
| `guardana.agent.mcp_server_manifest` | Live MCP tool manifest carries a hidden instruction or has drifted | HIGH | `probe --mcp URL` |

## System prompt and tool schema leaks

Guardana checks for system prompt leaks using a canary marker and disclosure of hidden tool schema context on request.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.prompt.system_prompt_leak.canary` | System prompt leakage via canary marker | CRITICAL | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |
| `guardana.agent.hidden_context.tool_schema` | Hidden context in a tool schema disclosed on request | HIGH | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |

## Secrets and cross-tenant data leaks

Guardana checks for secrets in model output, another tenant's seeded data in replies, cross-tenant document retrieval, and credentials in recorded tool arguments.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.output.secrets` | Secret leaked in model output | HIGH | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |
| `guardana.tenancy.cross_tenant_answer` | Another tenant's seeded data reached a reply | CRITICAL | `probe --url URL --model MODEL --fixtures FILE` |
| `guardana.trace.cross_tenant_retrieval` | A retrieval returned a document belonging to another tenant | CRITICAL | `analyze-trace TRACE` |
| `guardana.trace.secret_in_tool_argument` | A credential appeared in a recorded tool argument | HIGH | `analyze-trace TRACE` |

## Agent actions beyond authorization

Guardana checks for unsolicited destructive tool calls, overly broad tool arguments, planted secrets in tool arguments, actions taken despite denied or inconclusive policy decisions, and side effects without required approval.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.agent.excessive_tool_use` | Model invokes a destructive tool it was not asked to use | HIGH | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |
| `guardana.agent.tool_argument_scope` | Agent widens a tool argument beyond the task it was given | HIGH | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |
| `guardana.agent.credential_exfiltration` | Agent leaks a planted secret through a tool argument | CRITICAL | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |
| `guardana.trace.policy_decision_ignored` | An action a policy refused, or could not decide, went ahead | HIGH | `analyze-trace TRACE` |
| `guardana.trace.unapproved_side_effect` | A consequential effect executed without an approval that was recorded as needed | HIGH | `analyze-trace TRACE` |

## Unbounded output and costly requests

Guardana checks for unbounded output generation and cheap requests that are expensive to answer.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.prompt.unbounded_consumption` | Unbounded output generation (denial-of-wallet) | MEDIUM | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |
| `guardana.prompt.cost_asymmetry` | A cheap request that is expensive to answer (cost asymmetry) | MEDIUM | `probe --url URL --model MODEL` |

## Unauthenticated chat inference

Guardana checks, on request, whether the named chat completions route returns a completion to a caller without a credential.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.endpoint.unauthenticated_inference` | Chat route returns a completion to a caller without a credential | CRITICAL | `probe --url URL --model MODEL --api-key-env VAR --require-auth` |

## MCP access and registry weaknesses

Guardana checks for unauthenticated tool or task listings, unusable or unsafe discovery, issuer ambiguity, acceptance of foreign bearer tokens, weak sessions, broad scopes, publicly cacheable protected listings, and registry mismatches.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.mcp.unauthenticated_access` | MCP server answers a tool listing with no credential | HIGH | `probe --mcp URL` |
| `guardana.mcp.authorization_discovery` | Protected MCP server publishes no usable authorization surface | HIGH | `probe --mcp URL` |
| `guardana.mcp.token_audience` | MCP server accepts a bearer token it could not have issued | CRITICAL | `probe --mcp URL` |
| `guardana.mcp.session_binding` | MCP session id is guessable, or stands in for authentication | HIGH | `probe --mcp URL` |
| `guardana.mcp.scope_breadth` | MCP server advertises scopes that cannot express least privilege | MEDIUM | `probe --mcp URL` |
| `guardana.mcp.discovery_target` | MCP server directs its client to an address a client must not follow | HIGH | `probe --mcp URL` |
| `guardana.mcp.issuer_identification` | Authorization server gives an MCP client no way to detect an issuer mix-up | MEDIUM | `probe --mcp URL` |
| `guardana.mcp.cache_scope` | MCP server declares a credential-gated tool listing publicly cacheable | MEDIUM | `probe --mcp URL` |
| `guardana.mcp.task_identity` | MCP server shows tasks to a caller who presented no credential | HIGH | `probe --mcp URL` |
| `guardana.mcp.registry_entry` | MCP server is not the one its registry entry publishes | MEDIUM | `probe --mcp URL --mcp-registry-entry FILE` |

## A2A card and access weaknesses

Guardana checks for incomplete agent cards or requirements callers cannot meet, responses to callers without credentials, and tasks shown to callers who do not own them.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.a2a.agent_card` | A2A agent card is incomplete, or declares what no caller can satisfy | MEDIUM | `probe --a2a URL` |
| `guardana.a2a.caller_identity` | A2A agent answers a caller presenting no credential | HIGH | `probe --a2a URL` |
| `guardana.a2a.task_visibility` | A2A agent shows a task to a caller who does not own it | HIGH | `probe --a2a URL` |

## Delegation beyond granted authority

Guardana checks for credentials crossing trust boundaries, tokens used outside their audience, sessions used as credentials for state changes, scopes without recorded consent, and authority beyond a handoff.

| Rule | Reports | Default severity | Runs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guardana.trace.credential_passthrough` | A credential was presented across two different trust boundaries | HIGH | `analyze-trace TRACE` |
| `guardana.trace.identity_disagreement` | A token was presented to a resource outside its audience | HIGH | `analyze-trace TRACE` |
| `guardana.trace.session_as_identity` | A state-changing step was identified by a session rather than a credential | HIGH | `analyze-trace TRACE` |
| `guardana.trace.consent_scope_exceeded` | A scope was exercised that no consent record granted | HIGH | `analyze-trace TRACE` |
| `guardana.trace.handoff_authority_expansion` | An agent exercised more authority than the handoff carried to it | HIGH | `analyze-trace TRACE` |

## Prevent regressions

Use these checks to catch regressions in scans, live probes, and recorded runs.

- `guardana scan` exits `1` when a finding meets `fail_on` (HIGH by default) and `2` when required coverage is missing, blocking the merge in CI. Use the GitHub Action, a pre-commit hook, or GitLab, Jenkins, and Azure templates. See [integrations](../integrations.md).
- `guardana baseline` records accepted findings as waivers with a reason, approver, and expiry. With `scan --baseline`, new findings still fail the gate, and findings with expired waivers fail again if still present. See [baselines](../usage-baseline.md).
- `guardana diff accepted.json current.json` exits `1` if a finding appears, is proven, or escalates at or above the `fail_on` bar, or, at any severity, a check can no longer reach a verdict, a rule stops running, or a file leaves the scan. It exits `2` if the runs cannot be compared. See [run comparisons](../usage-diff.md).
- `guardana monitor` (beta) reruns endpoint rules with a fresh canary each cycle and alerts if the gate fails, more checks fail to run, or a cycle is worse than the first. See [endpoint monitoring](../usage-monitor.md).
- `guardana probe --mcp URL --write-mcp-pin PIN` saves the approved tool manifest. A later probe with `--mcp-pin PIN` reports changed tool declarations as CRITICAL. If the pin cannot be compared, the run ends indeterminate (exit `2`). See [MCP probes](../usage-probe.md).
- `guardana analyze-trace --contract FILE` checks recorded runs against 5 contract types (`tenant_boundary`, `approval_required`, `allowed_scopes`, `credential_boundary`, `forbidden_sink`). The run ends indeterminate (exit `2`) if the trace lacks evidence a contract needs. See [trace contracts](../usage-contracts.md).
